content.key_idea: Two Toffoli gates sharing one control qubit would normally run sequentially; decomposing each into T-gates and then using commutation rules to push matching-control CNOTs together turns them into parallel Fanout gates, cutting circuit depth without changing the T-depth.
content.reading_order: (a) first: a compact shared-control Toffoli pair expanded into its optimal T-gate decomposition; (b) the two commutation rules used to reorder gates; (c) the final circuit, read left to right through 8 numbered steps, where matching-control CNOTs from both decompositions have been merged into simultaneous Fanout gates

summary: This figure derives a parallel implementation of two shared-control Toffoli gates. Panel (a) expands the compact shared-control Toffoli pair (control qubit phi, targets rho_i/rho_j for each of two copies) into its optimal T-gate decomposition (7 T gates, T-depth 4), shaded blue for the first Toffoli and gold for the second. Panel (b) states two generic commutation rules: gates sharing a control commute regardless of vertical order, and a single-qubit rotation commutes past a CNOT it does not control. Panel (c) applies these rules to push the second decomposition's CNOTs and single-qubit gates backward until CNOTs that share the control qubit phi line up in the same step, merging into Fanout gates; the resulting 8-step circuit keeps the optimal T-depth of 4 while executing both Toffolis with far less overall depth than running them sequentially.
